summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this video, we will learn how to correctly use the auto-adjustment and auto-adjustment functions of the test suit. ## Creating a Test Suit First, let's learn how to create a test suit. You can import an OBJ file or FBX file as a virtual model. After importing an OBJ file, select the corresponding unit in the import window and then click OK. You can refer to the ratio of the characters and the ground in the video to select the unit to be imported—make sure it's not too big or too small. Next, we need a virtual model. Once we have created the test suit, it will start working as soon as we run out the total costume beneath the model. ### Important Note When creating the test suit, remember to zip it up so that when you select it, the costume will be emptied. Otherwise, when you select to create a test suit with the wide AO suit, the costume will not be emptied out. ## 3D Measurement and Model Creation After discussing the creation of the window, we need to follow the size of these parts according to the height to gradually create a 3D measurement line on the virtual model. - Click on three points on the virtual model to create a virtual model. - We will create it in slow motion. - Create the first starting point, then click on the second point. - When clicking on the third point, move the mouse to refer to the preview effect. - In the confirmed position, click on the third point to form a circle. When creating a circle measurement, press the Shift key to create a point along the level or value direction. If your model is left and right symmetrical, you can open the symmetrical creation key when dealing with the wrist. If not, cancel the selection of symmetry to separate the left and right side measurements. Continue to create other measurements in accordance with the sequence. If there is a mistake in the measurement data or adjustments are needed, you can click on the measurement, select delete, and create this measurement data again. ## Adjusting the Virtual Model If your model used in the video requires adjustments to the shoulder or some joint positions, you can do that as needed. In the bottom right corner, there is a leave-out option. Once all measurements have been created, click on the application, and these panels will be divided together to form a test fit. It should be tightly attached to the virtual model. If there are places where the virtual model penetrates, manually drag the panel so that it does not have a large amount of penetration. After the test fit is complete, click Save to save the virtual model. ## Using Auto-Adjustment Features Every time you want to use the self-adjustment panel or the self-adjustment function, import this model. Click on the 3D window to display the test fit of the virtual model. Here, you can see that there is already a circle of test fits around the virtual model. You can also choose to hide the virtual model test fit. Because there is a test fit on the model, you can import a test fit of the virtual model to perform other operations. In the file folder of the software, all virtual models have test fit information. To check whether a virtual model has test fit information, go to the virtual model display column and find the display virtual model test fit. After opening it, you will see the red test fit, indicating the test fit information of the virtual model itself. ### Test Fit Information Why is there test fit information in the pre-set file folder? Because these clothes are on the pre-set virtual model provided by the software, which has test fit information. Before simulating this suit, it always carries the original test fit information. You can compare the test fit information of the virtual model to perform automatic wear or automatic adjustment. These functions are all based on these two files, protecting their own test fit information. If you click on automatic wear, the suit will not calculate any adjustments, only wear it on the virtual model. Since it has remodeled the calculation, the test fit information it carries now is also the test fit information of this new model. ## Adjusting and Saving the Suit Press Ctrl + Z to revert to when the suit still carries the previous test fit information. Press Shift + F to open the arrangement point. Here, manually arrange the version and adjust its arrangement value so that there is no difference with the virtual model, then arrange the front and back pieces separately. Press the control key to simulate. This suit will still retain the test fit information of the virtual model. After confirming that the suit has the test fit information, save it in the upper left corner to use later. ## Situations Where Auto-Adjustment Cannot Be Used Let’s examine under what circumstances the automatic wear or automatic adjustment functions cannot be used. 1. **Missing Test Fit Information**: If you have a suit with test fit information but choose to import an OBJ model as a virtual model, the OBJ model will not automatically create a test fit. Thus, you will lack the test fit information of the virtual model. - If the test fit information is missing, clicking on the automatic wear or automatic adjustment version will pop up a prompt indicating that your virtual model needs to create a test fit first and register it. 2. **New Clothes Without Test Fit Information**: If your virtual model has test fit information but the clothes loaded do not have test fit information saved for the second time, the automatic adjustment version or automatic wear functions will not work. The software will prompt you that this costume must have test fit information. Sometimes, if you download a costume or create one without test fit information, you can use the virtual model file in the library window to bring in these pre-set virtual models from the folder. ## Final Steps To use these functions, remember to save this costume in the left-hand corner first, then upload it to your virtual model with test fit information. The virtual model provided by the software can be edited in the virtual model editor. When you edit the size of the virtual model, the test fit of the virtual model will also change accordingly. If using the Move Target function to transform the first OBJ model, the test fit information on the original OBJ model will also be transformed. ## Conclusion In this tutorial video, we demonstrated the correct way to use the automatic wearing or automatic adjustment version. Import a virtual model with test fit information, then open a costume with test fit information. You can see that after using the automatic wearing function, the costume will be fully worn on the virtual model. However, if there is a body size gap, the wearing effect may not be optimal. In such cases, you can use the automatic adjustment version function to calculate the body size difference and automatically adjust the version. The higher the value of the adjustment version, the more it maintains all the original curves. After confirming and clicking on the adjustment, wait for the calculation to complete, and the costume will automatically be worn on the new virtual model. This tutorial ends here. See you next time! Bye bye. ```
